hero.alt: Green title card reading Does Showering Count as Wudu?

sources.title: Egypt's Dar al-Ifta fatwa 24065: praying without ablution after a purificatory bath
sources.supports: Ablution is included within the purificatory bath; cites Aisha and Ibn Umar; prayer valid.

sources.title: Sunan Abi Dawud 250: performing wudu after ghusl
sources.supports: Aisha: the Prophet bathed and prayed without performing ablution afresh; graded sahih by al-Albani.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 248: ablution before taking a bath
sources.supports: The Prophet's ghusl after janabah began with ablution like that for prayer.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwa 03298: Fardh and Sunnah of Ghusl
sources.supports: Hanafi: three fardh acts of ghusl; Sunnah acts include intention and wudu before ghusl.

sources.title: Qur'an 5:6 (Al-Ma'idah)
sources.supports: Wudu for prayer and full bath for major impurity in one verse.

review.notes: Re-read each retrieved page text captured 2026-10-27: Dar al-Ifta fatwa 24065, Abu Dawud 250 (sahih per al-Albani), Bukhari 248, Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwa 03298 and Qur'an 5:6. Tirmidhi 107 returned 403 and is not cited; Aisha's report and Ibn Umar's comment are attributed via the Dar al-Ifta fatwa that quotes them. Jordanian and other non-allowlisted fatwas were not used. No ruling is given on whether a plain non-ghusl shower lifts minor impurity: readers are advised to make wudu or ask a scholar. Hanafi fardh list attributed to that school. Hero inspected: 1200x630 meadow-palette title card, not duplicated in body. No app CTA; links /prayer-times and existing guides.

claim_checks.claim: Ablution is included within the purificatory bath; intention for major impurity covers minor; funeral prayer valid
claim_checks.explanation: Answer: 'It is established in Islamic law that ablution is included within the purificatory bath... the lesser is included in the intention of the greater'; prayer valid.

claim_checks.claim: Aisha: Prophet would not make ablution after the bath; Ibn Umar: 'You have gone beyond what is necessary'
claim_checks.explanation: Both reports quoted in the fatwa.

claim_checks.claim: Aisha: he bathed, prayed two rak'ahs and the dawn prayer, 'I do not think he performed ablution afresh after taking a bath'; sahih per al-Albani
claim_checks.explanation: Exact English text and grade Sahih (Al-Albani) on page.

claim_checks.claim: Prophet's ghusl after janabah: washed hands, 'then performed ablution like that for the prayer', then poured water over head and body
Qur'an 5:6 mentions washing limbs for prayer and full bath for major impurity
claim_checks.explanation: 'wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet... if you are in a state of full impurity, then take a full bath.'

claim_checks.claim: Hanafi fardh of ghusl: rinse mouth, water into nose and blow out, wash whole body; missing any leaves obligation; Sunnah includes Bismillah, intention, wudu before ghusl
claim_checks.explanation: Fatwa 03298 lists the three fardh and nine Sunnah acts verbatim.
